patch.value: GH-891: external blockers make graph stale_lifecycle_block impossible to resolve truthfully

GitHub issue #891 reports that pm graph audit treats blocked work without an open tracker predecessor as stale even when blocked_reason precisely documents a real external party or event that should not be fabricated as a PM item. The audit needs an honest first-class external-blocker policy or a blocked_reason-backed classification so machine governance remains actionable.

The SDK governance policy distinguishes missing blocker evidence from documented external blockers without inventing graph nodes; CLI, SDK, MCP, contracts, docs, and tests expose one deterministic externally-blocked representation and severity policy; The existing genuinely stale blocked case remains actionable and a negative control proves the audit still catches it
pm-cli 2026.8.3; external fleet tracker; pm graph audit --json

Create or inspect a blocked item with a precise non-empty blocked_reason and no internal ordering predecessor; run pm graph audit --json; observe stale_lifecycle_block with remediation that requires fabricating or reopening a tracker item
Externally blocked work has a truthful machine-readable representation and does not emit an actionable stale-lifecycle defect when its evidence is complete
The audit reports stale_lifecycle_block and recommends an internal edge or active status even when neither is truthful
Agents learn to ignore graph audits or fabricate placeholder work, weakening governance and context truth
